signals.title: The Two Genie Game: Adoption and Welfare in Audit-Grounded AI Governance
signals.summary: We ask under what conditions an agent with a harm-minimizing policy can displace an approval-seeking (RLHF) agent in a competitive market, and when that policy is sufficient to prevent community harm. We use evolutionary game theory (finite-population Moran-Fermi pairwise comparison) to formalize this subject to assumptions of wisher hindsight, peer testimony, a monotone harm ledger, sufficient information density of community feedback, and a finite, depleting resource pool, in a negative-sum environment.
signals.implication: Reassess role boundaries and human override for community deployments. Update constitutional clauses and compliance mappings for community operators. High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: The article discusses the conditions under which an agent following a harm-minimizing policy might outperform an approval-seeking agent in a competitive environment. It employs evolutionary game theory techniques, specifically a finite-population Moran-Fermi model, to analyze these dynamics under various assumptions. Key elements include wisher hindsight, peer testimony, a monotone harm ledger, adequate community feedback, and a limited resource pool within a negative-sum scenario. This study could provide insights on the governance policies necessary to mitigate community harm while fostering competitive fairness among AI agents. Understanding such dynamics is crucial for a community focused on AI, as it informs how to develop policies that balance innovation with ethical considerations.

signals.title: Structure-Preserving Document Translation via Multi-Stage LLM Pipeline: A Case Study in Marathi
